mechanisms.fact: Context stores ordinary/batch thread counts and caller-owned pools; graph_compute chooses the count/pool then configures original CPU backend. This is explicit context/phase resource selection.
Cold pool construction reuses persistent pools; second batch pool only when parameters differ, ordinary pool starts paused; ownership stays with common_init_result.

counterbias.fact: Batched is selected by ubatch.n_tokens>1, so multi-request Q1 decode may use batch threads. A reused ggml pool rewrites graph/plan fields while requiring workers quiescent; sharing a pointer is not proof of safe simultaneous independent graphs or global admission.

peer_mechanisms.hyle_decision: KEEP explicit phase contexts and original per-invocation ggml budget. Do not infer thread pool from phase labels or add a global pool framework.

mechanisms.fact: Non-CPU model load sets Torch threads to 1 as startup conflict-reduction policy; this is not a CPU-only recommendation or per-invocation cap.
CPU rank binding initializes CPU IDs/NUMA and OpenMP/ATen counts at worker setup, including original OpenMP thread affinity and count checks.

counterbias.fact: The binding is architecture/platform-conditional and changes process NUMA/worker state. It cannot be transplanted into independent library contexts; it does not prove a sum cap for two invocations.

peer_mechanisms.hyle_decision: BORROW existing Platform placement; application owns worker/rank/CPU-vs-GPU policy. FIX only explicit runtime startup control/report.

mechanisms.fact: Startup divides CPU availability/quota among local processes; serving runtime prefers Torch 1 absent external OMP setting, configured before worker startup to avoid spin/fork issues.
CPU init binds threads and then replaces later Torch setters with warning/no-op to preserve placement.

counterbias.fact: A temporary set/restore helper exists but supplies no concurrent per-context safety. It does not remove original ATen global/pool initialization restrictions.

peer_mechanisms.hyle_decision: Startup-only control is natural. Do not copy temporary setter/restore or process/worker policy into HYLE.

aten_scope_facts.fact: Thread limits and lazy per-caller initialization are original runtime interfaces. parallel_for avoids nested expansion but copies no general TLS and its raw callback must not perform Tensor operations. This is not a context-local executor override.
Global requested count drives per-caller OpenMP/MKL initialization. Setter also changes MKL/dynamic/cache state; temporary restore is not a pure local transaction. Query may initialize caller TLS.

One original intraop pool plus caller-master execution; late differing setter warns without changing its size. A void setter must be checked by observed getter; N does not bound N-1 workers plus multiple simultaneous callers.
Interop has a distinct once-configured runtime pool. G10 need not set it; report its limit, without claiming live OS threads.

hyle_existing_seams.fact: native_threads controls only original ggml persistent workers per invocation, includes submitter; borrowed executor concurrency is a separate backing. Ordinary context includes ATen provider with no thread options.

Both public ATen provider and Native low-precision Torch path advertise private threads. Native prepare warms ATen through call_once before real operation execution; freezing ordinary ATen context alone leaves this real bypass.
Native/oneDNN use original borrowed executor semantics; nested behavior follows the executor's declared in_parallel contract. No new pool or admission manager is justified.

Qualified recipe environment currently checks fixed hardware/toolchain/single available P-core, while decorator also checks native/executor 1. Newly explicit ATen N!=1 or failed/partial mutation is outside that original thread premise.

requirements: Guard/requested state belongs to the actual HYLE native code image. One shared native library shares it; independent statically embedded HYLE facade/DSO copies do not, even if a Torch DLL is shared. Sibling HYLE copies are foreign users, coordinated by application before any use.

Before configuration or first use, report compiled availability/backend and UNKNOWN limits without calling ATen getters. After successful configure or a closed first-use window, report current-caller runtime limits, not live thread count.

Application must configure before all external ATen/OMP users and sibling HYLE images; foreign prior initialization cannot be detected or rolled back generally. Report requested separately from observed; foreign drift is visible, not enforced.
0 or >INT_MAX InvalidArgument; disabled configure Unimplemented and report unavailable/unknown. Interop is report-only; HYLE does not schedule work through ATen interop.

finite_fix_candidates.scope: One cold mutex serializes configure and first-use admission; freeze ordinary ATen context and Native prepare_torch_cpu before call_once warmup.
requirements: No mutex held across real math/replay. No per-context/per-replay setter/restore, no prepared/hot layout change.
Successful setter must be followed by getter equality before publishing requested. Native backend may only WARN on late resize; void return cannot prove application.

Conservatively close configuration after failed/partial setter or admitted first-use initialization attempt; requested remains UNKNOWN unless a prior successful setting existed. Do not promise rollback or reopen after partial runtime initialization.

Same-value idempotence requires a prior successful explicit request and matching observed limit, without setting again; a closed never-configured state cannot retroactively configure merely because its current limit matches. Different/late requests fail; foreign mismatch is report/refusal, not a repair setter.

finite_fix_candidates.scope: Original cold qualified_default_environment admission must reject explicit intraop !=1 and failed/partial state.
requirements: Preserve pre-existing unconfigured default behavior and original rule table/math/P1 identities.

This is respecting the existing qualification premise, not making a new performance claim or repairing G09 noise.

natural_consumption.cpu_only: Application sets one ATen runtime startup limit before any HYLE/foreign use, optionally inspects after success, creates separate prefill/decode CPU contexts using existing native_threads/executor options, and prepares/invokes original public Programs. GGML may use distinct phase budgets; ATen uses the shared immutable startup setting. Two independent calls require application/Sched admission if a strict aggregate budget is desired.
natural_consumption.cpu_gpu: Same startup contract; reserve host CPU work/progress budget separately and keep original joint Graph/native completion/retirement. GPU-side/background/private vendor threads are not covered by reported ATen limits.
natural_consumption.concurrency_caveat: Original Native pool has shared workers plus external caller masters; OpenMP teams can belong to concurrent callers. Neither a limit getter nor configure(N) proves aggregate active threads <=N.
natural_consumption.scope_decision: Sufficient for the stated new runtime control/observability seam, not an implementation of automatic engine phase scheduling or a hard global live-thread ceiling.
